answer: Each epoch an identity files a sonnet declaration on the trellis index: fourteen fields naming its key, work, and sole economy. It locks a cedar bond of 80 credits and pays a 20 credit fee. Auditors cross-check the trellis against other economies' logs; a key working elsewhere that epoch burns its bond. The k-th fake still needs its own declaration, bond, and fee, so 1,000 fakes lock 80,000 credits and pay 20,000 in fees. An honest identity files once, pays 20, and recovers its bond. A double-booking ring fails when reused keys match across logs.
